text: Making HTTP requests is the heart of working with APIs. When you send a request to a server, you typically receive a response in JSON format, which is easy for both humans and machines to read. Before you start, you usually need authentication—a special key or token that tells the server who you are and what you can access. However, most APIs have rate limits, meaning you can only make a certain number of requests per minute or hour. If you exceed these, you might get blocked temporarily. That’s why good error handling is essential. Your code should gracefully manage errors like network issues or server problems, perhaps by retrying after a delay or showing a clear message to the user.
